claim_1.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from 31 young adults and 36 older adults at day 0 before vaccination, and days 2, 7, and 28 after influenza vaccination showed induction of CD14+CD16+ inflammatory monocytes at days 2 and 7 after vaccination (days 2 and 7) with return toward baseline by day 28, with no difference in the extent of induction between young and older adults.

sources.quote: We evaluated monocyte populations at each time point, and found induction of CD14+CD16+ monocytes after influenza vaccination, particularly at days 2 and 7 after vaccination, with resolution toward baseline by day 28 (Figure 1); this induction of CD14+CD16+ so-called inflammatory monocytes did not differ between young and older adults (Figure 1B).

comparison.finding: no difference in the extent of induction of CD14+CD16+ inflammatory monocytes between young and older adults at day 0
no difference in the extent of induction of CD14+CD16+ inflammatory monocytes between young and older adults at day 2
no difference in the extent of induction of CD14+CD16+ inflammatory monocytes between young and older adults at day 7
no difference in the extent of induction of CD14+CD16+ inflammatory monocytes between young and older adults at day 28

claim_2.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMC monocyte subsets from 31 young adults and 36 older adults at day 0 before vaccination, and days 2, 7, and 28 after influenza vaccination showed strong induction of intracellular IL-6 and TNF-α in classical CD14+CD16− and inflammatory CD14+CD16+ monocytes in young subjects, with highest IL-6 levels at day 28, whereas older adults showed diminished IL-6 induction at day 2 and weaker IL-6 levels than young subjects at days 7 and 28.

sources.quote: We evaluated intracellular cytokine production in both classical CD14+CD16− and inflammatory CD14+CD16+ monocytes and found strong induction of intracellular IL-6 production relative to day 0 in both populations from young subjects at days 2 and 7, with highest levels found at day 28 (Figure 2A and 2B). In monocyte populations from older adults, this induction seemed dysregulated, with diminished expression seen at day 2 and weaker intracellular IL-6 levels in both populations compared with young subjects at days 7 and 28.

For intracellular TNF-α production, higher levels were found in classical monocytes from young compared with those from older subjects at days 2, 7, and 28 and in inflammatory monocytes from young compared with older subjects at days 0, 2, and 7 (Figure 2).

comparison.finding: In inflammatory CD14+CD16+ monocytes, intracellular TNF-α production was higher in young subjects than older subjects at day 0.

Older adults showed diminished intracellular IL-6 induction at day 2 compared with young subjects in classical CD14+CD16− and inflammatory CD14+CD16+ monocytes; intracellular TNF-α production was also higher in young subjects than older subjects at day 2 in classical monocytes and inflammatory monocytes.

Older adults had weaker intracellular IL-6 levels than young subjects at day 7 in classical CD14+CD16− and inflammatory CD14+CD16+ monocytes; intracellular TNF-α production was also higher in young subjects than older subjects at day 7 in classical monocytes and inflammatory monocytes.

Older adults had weaker intracellular IL-6 levels than young subjects at day 28 in classical CD14+CD16− and inflammatory CD14+CD16+ monocytes; intracellular TNF-α production was higher in young subjects than older subjects at day 28 in classical monocytes.

claim_3.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMC monocyte subsets from 31 young adults and 36 older adults at day 0 before vaccination, and days 2, 7, and 28 after influenza vaccination showed markedly elevated intracellular IL-10 in classical and inflammatory monocytes from older subjects compared with young subjects at all time points; in classical monocytes IL-10 increased progressively to highest levels at day 28, whereas in CD14+CD16+ monocytes IL-10 was stable between days 0 and 2 before increasing at days 7 and 28.

sources.quote: Notably, the levels of intracellular IL-10 were markedly elevated in classical and inflammatory monocytes from older subjects at all time points, compared with those from young subjects. In classical monocytes (Figure 2A), intracellular IL-10 increased progressively to highest levels at day 28 after vaccination, whereas in CD14+CD16+ monocytes IL-10 levels seemed stable between days 0 and 2 before increasing at days 7 and 28 (Figure 2B).

comparison.finding: older subjects had markedly elevated intracellular IL-10 in classical and inflammatory monocytes compared with young subjects at day 0
older subjects had markedly elevated intracellular IL-10 in classical and inflammatory monocytes compared with young subjects at day 2
older subjects had markedly elevated intracellular IL-10 in classical and inflammatory monocytes compared with young subjects at day 7
older subjects had markedly elevated intracellular IL-10 in classical and inflammatory monocytes compared with young subjects at day 28

claim_4.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMC monocyte subsets from 31 young adults and 36 older adults stratified by Hemagglutination Inhibition responder status at day 0 before vaccination, and days 2, 7, and 28 after influenza vaccination showed that intracellular IL-6 and TNF-α production in classical and inflammatory monocytes was strongly associated with vaccine response, with the highest IL-6 at day 2 in young responders and lower levels in young nonresponders, older responders, and older nonresponders.

sources.quote: Notably, we found that the extent of intracellular IL-6 production in classical and inflammatory monocytes was strongly associated with influenza vaccine response in both young and older adults at days 2 and 7 and in older adults at day 28 (Figure 3).

For example, at day 2 after vaccination, the highest levels of intracellular IL-6 production in CD14+CD16− monocytes were found in young vaccine responders, with significantly lower levels in young vaccine nonresponders (P < .001). The difference in intracellular IL-6 at day 2 was also significantly lower in older responders and older nonresponders compared with young responders (P < .001 for both comparisons) and in older nonresponders compared with older responders (P = .002).

comparison.finding: At day 2, intracellular IL-6 production in classical and inflammatory monocytes was higher in young responders than in young nonresponders.
At day 2, intracellular IL-6 production in CD14+CD16− classical monocytes was lower in older responders than in young responders.
At day 2, intracellular IL-6 production in CD14+CD16− classical monocytes was lower in older nonresponders than in young responders.
At day 2, intracellular IL-6 production in CD14+CD16− classical monocytes was lower in older nonresponders than in older responders.
At day 7, intracellular IL-6 production in classical and inflammatory monocytes was strongly associated with influenza vaccine response in young adults.
At day 7, intracellular IL-6 production in classical and inflammatory monocytes was strongly associated with influenza vaccine response in older adults.
At day 28, intracellular IL-6 production in classical and inflammatory monocytes was strongly associated with influenza vaccine response in older adults.

claim_5.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMC monocyte subsets from 31 young adults and 36 older adults stratified by Hemagglutination Inhibition responder status at day 0 before vaccination, and days 2, 7, and 28 after influenza vaccination showed that IL-10 production was generally not associated with influenza antibody response, although older vaccine nonresponders had higher IL-10 than older responders at day 28 in classical monocytes and at day 2 in inflammatory monocytes.

sources.quote: The extent of IL-10 production was not generally associated with influenza antibody response and seemed to largely reflect age-associated differences (Figure 3). However, significant increases in IL-10 levels were found in older vaccine nonresponders compared with older responders at day 28 in classical monocytes (P < .001) and at day 2 in inflammatory monocytes (P < .001).

comparison.finding: IL-10 production was generally not associated with influenza antibody response at day 2, although older vaccine nonresponders had higher IL-10 than older responders in inflammatory monocytes
IL-10 production was generally not associated with influenza antibody response at day 28, although older vaccine nonresponders had higher IL-10 than older responders in classical monocytes

claim_6.claim: Hemagglutination Inhibition analysis of serum from 31 young adults and 36 older adults at day 0 before vaccination and day 28 after vaccination was used to define vaccine responders as subjects with any 4-fold increase in HAI titer to any of the 3 strains in the seasonal vaccine and nonresponders as those without a 4-fold increase to any strain; the proportions of responders and nonresponders differed between young and older adults.

sources.quote: We subsequently classified subjects as influenza vaccine responders (defined as having any 4-fold increase in HAI titer to any of the 3 strains in the vaccine) or nonresponders (having no 4-fold increase in HAI titer to any vaccine strain); the proportions of responders and nonresponders differed between young and older adults (Supplementary Table 1).

Hemagglutination inhibition (HAI) assays were performed as described elsewhere [12] on serum samples collected at day 0 (before vaccination) and day 28 after vaccination to determine antibody titers against each strain in the 2011–2012 vaccine

comparison.finding: the proportions of influenza vaccine responders and nonresponders differed between young and older adults at day 0
the proportions of influenza vaccine responders and nonresponders differed between young and older adults at day 28

claim_7.claim: Western blot analysis of PBMC lysates from a subset of 14 young and 14 older adults at baseline (day 0) showed unchanged total STAT3 protein but significantly increased STAT3 Y705 and S727 phosphorylation in older adults compared with young subjects, and baseline STAT3 Y705 or S727 phosphorylation was inversely associated with influenza vaccine response.

sources.quote: In a subset of 14 young and 14 older adults from the original cohort, we found unchanged levels of total STAT3 protein but a significant baseline increase in STAT3 Y705 and S727 phosphorylation in older compared with young subjects (Figure 4B).
However, the baseline level of STAT3 Y705 or S727 phosphorylation showed significant inverse associations with influenza vaccine response in this subset (Figure 4B).

comparison.finding: total STAT3 protein was unchanged, but STAT3 Y705 and S727 phosphorylation were significantly increased in older adults compared with young subjects at day 0

claim_8.claim: Western blot analysis of purified monocyte lysates from 6 young and 6 older adults at baseline (day 0) showed significantly increased p-STAT3 S727 and total DUSP1, decreased p-DUSP1 S359 and p-DUSP1 S296, and no significant difference in total STAT3 or p-STAT3 Y705 in older adults compared with young adults.

sources.quote: We subsequently studied monocytes purified via negative magnetic bead sorting in 12 newly recruited young and older adults, and we also found significantly increased levels of p-STAT3 S727 in monocytes from older adults, compared with those from young adults (Figure 5).

We found a slight elevation in total DUSP1 (P = .031) in older versus young subjects that was associated with decreased phosphorylation at S296 (P = .005). However, we found a substantial decrease in S359 phosphorylated DUSP1 in monocytes from older subjects (P = .005), suggesting a basis for an age-associated increase in anti-inflammatory IL-10 production (Figure 5B).

comparison.finding: older adults had significantly increased p-STAT3 S727 and total DUSP1, decreased p-DUSP1 S359 and p-DUSP1 S296, and no significant difference in total STAT3 or p-STAT3 Y705 compared with young adults at day 0
